places.name: The Grand Palace
places.ai_summary: A historic complex of buildings that served as the official residence of the Kings of Siam since 1782.

opening_hours.notes: Closed during royal ceremonies.

places.place_tip: Wear modest clothing as it is a sacred site.
places.address: Na Phra Lan Rd, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand

places.name: Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha)
places.ai_summary: A sacred Buddhist temple housing the Emerald Buddha, a highly revered religious artifact in Thailand.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited early morning to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Photography is restricted inside the temple. Respect the rules.
places.address: Na Phra Lan Rd, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand

places.name: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn)
places.ai_summary: A riverside temple known for its stunning spires and beautiful views during sunrise and sunset.

opening_hours.notes: Climbing the central prang offers panoramic views.

places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes for climbing the steep steps.
places.address: 158 Wang Doem Rd, Wat Arun, Bangkok, Thailand

attribution.title: King's Standard of Thailand
attribution.author: Tangmo
attribution.description: King's Standard of Thailand. This flag was first adopted by King Vajiravudh in 1910. This flag features red dancing Garuda on the yellow square.

places.name: Wat Pho (Reclining Buddha)
places.ai_summary: Famous for the giant reclining Buddha statue, this temple is a must-visit for its impressive architecture and serene atmosphere.

opening_hours.notes: The temple is also a traditional Thai massage school.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the massage school for an authentic experience.
places.address: 2 Sanam Chai Rd, Grand Palace Subdistrict, Prana Nakhon District, Bangkok, Thailand

Own work based on: https://www.nstda.or.th/th/nstda-knowledge/11557-thaiflag-color

Construction sheet of the flag of Thailand
attribution.description:
The national flag of Kingdom of Thailand; there are total of 3 colours:
Red represents the blood spilt to protect Thailand’s independence and often more simply described as representing the nation.
White represents the religion of Buddhism, the predominant religion of the nation
Blue represents the monarchy of the nation, which is recognised as the centre of Thai hearts.

places.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
places.ai_summary: One of the world's largest weekend markets, offering a vast array of goods from clothing to antiques.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Bargaining is expected. Keep your belongings secure.
places.address: Chatuchak, Bangkok, Thailand

places.name: Khaosan Road
places.ai_summary: A famous street known for its vibrant nightlife, street food, and budget accommodations.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the evening for nightlife.

places.place_tip: Watch out for tuk-tuk scams. Negotiate prices beforehand.
places.address: Khaosan Rd, Talat Yot, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
